definitions.I(G;z): sum over independent vertex sets X of z^|X|

identities: For child components rooted at c: A_u=product_c(A_c+z*B_c), B_u=product_c A_c.

For a leaf v adjacent to support s, root T at s and let C_u be the component on each other neighbor branch u after deleting s; J_u=I(C_u;z), A_u=I(C_u-u;z). Then I(T-v;z)=product_(u!=v)J_u + z*product_(u!=v)A_u.
For the same tagged leaf: I(T-{v,s};z)=product_(u!=v)J_u.
For the same tagged leaf: I(T-N[s];z)=product_(u non-leaf-neighbor of s)A_u.
verification: Each identity follows from unique independent-set decomposition by branches and, at a rooted vertex, by whether the root is included. Products are over disjoint components. The last identity removes s and every neighbor; each non-leaf branch root u is removed and leaves C_u-u, while pendant neighbors leave no component. Empty products equal 1.
limitation: Identities give exact finite-input evaluation only. They do not prove a coefficient inequality for the selected sum or provide a uniform state invariant controlling the global first strict descent and favorable selectors.
